newsitem.title: BULGARIA: World Bank pledges $170 mln Bulgaria loan in July.
newsitem.headline: World Bank pledges $170 mln Bulgaria loan in July.

text.p: The World Bank is expected to approve $170 million loans for Bulgaria in July after reviewing the country's reform performance, a bank official said on Thursday.

"It has become evident that the momentum is tremendous and I would be able to return to Washington and prepare the technical mission with full confidence that we will be able to bring this transaction to successful conclusion," World Bank mission leader Kenneth Lay told reporters.
Lay arrived in Sofia on Monday to ensure that the new reformist government which took office last month will continue the fast pace of structural reform started by the interim cabinet in March.

"Our current assistant strategy provides for $100 million financing now and to support the further progress of reforms we have under consideration a second FESAL of about $70 million," said Lay, after meeting with Prime Minister Ivan Kostov.
The Bank has earmarked some $170 million funding to Sofia under its Financial Enterprise Sectoral Adjustment Loan (FESAL) of total $290 million credits intended for Sofia this year.
A World Bank technical mission is expected to arrive shortly to review Bulgaria's progress in privatisation and closing down loss-making state firms.
The World Bank and the government smoothed differences over grain policy after the Bank agreed on a temporary 15 percent grain export tax earlier this week to offset further grain imports.

"We have arrived at an understanding that provides for an export tax to be applied on temporary basis with a provision for a phase out that will work out a fuly liberalised price and trade regime in agriculture," said Lay.
Bulgaria freed prices and trade rules on in line with agreements with multylaterals, but pending grain imports have prompted the government to seek partial protectionist measures.

"We have also had the opportunity to lay the foundation for a country assisted strategy. We are looking forward to estabilishing an evironment of growth and improving the standards of living of Bulgarians," said Lay. -- Elisaveta Konstantinova, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-981-4145
